classification.difficultyReason: Apply the LCM to recurring events, convert minutes to seconds and include the initial simultaneous flash.

content.prompt: Standing on the seashore, Stephanie can see two ships’ lights flashing. One light flashes at intervals of 12 seconds and the other at intervals of 18 seconds.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If they flash together once, how long is it before they flash together again?

answer.worked:
Multiples of $12$: $12,24,36,48,\ldots$

Multiples of $18$: $18,36,54,\ldots$

The lowest common multiple is $36$, so they flash together again after 36 seconds.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If they flash together at the start of a 5-minute interval, how many times will they flash together in those 5 minutes?

answer.short: 9 times, including the flash at the start.
answer.worked:
$5$ minutes is $5\times60=300$ seconds.

The simultaneous flashes occur at $0,36,72,108,144,180,216,252,288$ seconds. The next would be at $324$ seconds, outside the interval.

Including the flash at the start, they flash together 9 times.
